author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Hundreds of runners and walkers gathered in East Providence on Saturday for the Mark Palumbo Memorial University Orthopedics 5K, raising support for the Tomorrow Fund at Hasbro Children’s Hospital. The course began near the University Orthopedics Surgery Center at Kettle Point along the East Bay Bike Path.

The Tomorrow Fund provides financial and emotional assistance to children undergoing cancer treatment and to their families. NBC 10 reported that the 5K has raised more than $250,000 for the organization since the event was dedicated to Dr. Mark Palumbo’s memory in 2021, making the annual race a continuing source of local support.

Saturday’s turnout connected a community fitness event with practical help for families facing long treatment schedules and related costs. University Orthopedics organized the race, while the beneficiary’s work is centered at Rhode Island’s pediatric hospital. The event’s cumulative fundraising reflects several years of participation from runners, sponsors, volunteers and medical-community partners.
dek: Hundreds joined the Mark Palumbo Memorial race, which has generated more than $250,000 for families facing childhood cancer since 2021.
headline: East Providence 5K boosts Hasbro Children’s Tomorrow Fund
